_doc: The VALIDITY oracle for every shipped generator (MCR-SEC-015 / MCR-SEC-021, conditions E1 and E6).
_why: tests/hostile_harness.js proved CONTAINMENT and nothing else: every hostile value is rejected or confined to one single-quoted shell token whose skeleton matches the benign control. It never asserted that the benign control is a VALID invocation of its tool, which is exactly how 20 short-option tokens joined with '=' across 11 of 24 generators passed 76,225 checks. This table is the missing oracle. Every row states the exact command a generator must emit for a stated set of benign values, on a stated release.
_authority: Hand-authored from each tool's own man page and getopt(3) semantics — NEVER generated from the assembler. A table regenerated from the code it tests is a transcript, not an oracle. When a row and the assembler disagree, the row is presumed right until the man page says otherwise.
_rules_pinned: A GNU long option takes its argument as --name=value (or --name value); both are accepted by getopt_long, and this product emits the '=' form.

A single-dash SHORT option takes its argument as '-X value' or glued as '-Xvalue'. It NEVER takes '-X=value': getopt(3) passes the '=' through as the first character of optarg. `chage -M=60` sets maxdays to the string '=60'; `auditctl -w=/etc/motd` watches nothing; `useradd -c=RFC-1234 -s=/bin/bash` sets a wrong GECOS and an invalid login shell without erroring.

A bare option with no argument (auditctl's -w value aside: `sshd -T`, `useradd -m`, `usermod -a`, `podman ps -a`, `setsebool -P`, `lvextend -r`, `firewall-cmd --permanent`, `journalctl --no-pager`, `journalctl --boot`) is emitted as its own word.
Every operator-supplied value is single-quoted, on both sides of the join. That is MCR-SEC-004 and it does not change here.
_completeness: The harness fails if a generator entry in content/commands.json has no row here, and fails if a row here names a generator that does not exist. A new generator cannot ship without stating the command it produces.
_null_means: commands.<release> === null means the generator is gated off that release and assembleCommand() must return null — not a shortened command.

_enum_branches._why: MCR-SEC-021, condition E6. benignFor() took opts[0], so the control value was always the first option — 'install', never 'remove'; 'start', never 'stop' or 'disable'. The destructive branch of every action enum was therefore never the benign control and its blast interaction was never asserted. The harness now sweeps every option of every enum field of every generator on every release, and every option named here must come out at least yellow.
_enum_branches._not_listed: 'restart' and 'reload' are disruptive but not destructive: they are offered only by gen-systemctl-manage, which is DECLARED yellow, so listing them here would assert nothing the declaration does not already carry. The list is for branches whose rating has to be EARNED on a generator declared green — as of G4(d) (Eli Cross's ruling raising gen-dnf-package/gen-yum-package's declared blast to yellow, closing exactly this gap), no shipped generator with a 'remove'/'stop'/'disable'/'off' branch is declared green any more, so the _control assertion below has nothing to check against today and is kept for the day a new destructive-branch generator lands declared green, rather than earning its own raise.
_enum_branches._control: For a generator declared green with a destructive branch, the sweep also requires that some branch comes out GREEN. A pattern table that rated everything yellow would satisfy the destructive assertion while proving nothing.

gen-fw-open-port.pins: --add-rich-rule= carries the composed rule as one single-quoted word; the rule's own grammar is checked by the rich-rule oracle

gen-nmcli-static-ipv4.pins: nmcli takes property/value PAIRS, not options: every setting name is an unquoted literal followed by a quoted value

gen-journalctl-unit-logs.pins: four long options keep the '=' join; --boot is a conditional bare option literal

gen-lsblk-inspect-storage.pins: -o is a short option and takes its curated column list as the next shell word. NAME stays first so lsblk preserves dependency-tree output on RHEL 7-10; MOUNTPOINT is the all-release oracle while the MOUNTPOINTS enum branch is gated to RHEL 9/10.

gen-pvcreate-initialize.pins: the block-device path is a validated absolute positional argument

gen-vgcreate-new-vg.pins: the volume-group name and block-device path are validated positional arguments

gen-lvcreate-new-lv.pins: lvcreate(8): -L takes a size and -n a name, both space-joined; the volume group is the trailing positional argument

gen-lvextend-grow.pins: lvextend(8): -L takes a size (the '+' prefix means GROW BY rather than SET TO); -r is a bare option and the LV path is positional

gen-sshd-test-config.pins: sshd(8): -T is bare, -f takes the config path space-joined

gen-useradd-create.pins: useradd(8): -m is bare; -c (GECOS), -G (groups) and -s (shell) are space-joined. The '=' join silently sets GECOS to '=RFC-1234' and the login shell to '=/bin/bash' without an error — MCR-SEC-015's second unsafe case.

gen-usermod-add-group.pins: usermod(8): -a is bare and MUST accompany -G, or -G REPLACES every supplementary group; -G is space-joined

gen-systemctl-query.pins: systemctl takes a SUBCOMMAND and a unit, both positional; a POSIX shell removes the quoting before execve so argv[1] is the bare word

gen-systemctl-manage.pins: same shape as the query generator; every branch of the action enum is swept separately for blast

gen-dnf-package.pins: dnf does not exist on RHEL 7 — null, not a shortened command

gen-yum-package.pins: yum is offered on all four releases (RHEL 8+ aliases it to dnf)

gen-setsebool-set.pins: setsebool(8): -P is a bare option meaning PERSISTENT. It is conditional on the persist field, and it is an OPTION, not an argument slot — dropping it shifts nothing (MCR-SEC-018 / MCR-SEC-022).

gen-semanage-port-add.pins: semanage-port(8): 'port' and '-a' are literals; -t (type) and -p (protocol) are space-joined; the port is positional

gen-chage-list.pins: chage(1): -l is bare and the user name is positional. Benign value 'adm-linux' (J1, VER-001 exposure): 'svcacct' does not exist on either lab host, so the receipted capture ran 'adm-linux' instead (documented in the capture's field_substitutions) — the golden row is pinned to the value that was actually, verifiably run.

gen-chage-set-aging.pins: chage(1): -M/-m/-W each take a number, space-joined. `chage -M=60` errors with "invalid numeric argument '=60'" — loud, but still wrong.

gen-auditctl-watch.pins: auditctl(8): -w (watch path), -p (permissions) and -k (key) are all space-joined. This is MCR-SEC-015's worst case: `auditctl -w='/etc/motd'` does NOT error in a way an operator recognises, so a STIG control is recorded as applied when no watch exists.

gen-ausearch-by-key.pins: ausearch(8): -k and -ts are MULTI-CHARACTER single-dash options and still take their argument space-joined, never with '='

gen-rsyslogd-test-config.pins: rsyslogd(8): -N1 is a glued short option written as a single literal token; -f is space-joined

gen-chronyd-one-shot-check.pins: chronyd(8) SYNOPSIS is `chronyd [OPTION]... [DIRECTIVE]...`: -Q takes NO argument, and the configuration directive is an OPERAND accepted after the options, so it is a separate quoted word after -Q rather than -Q's value. Same emitted command either way; the distinction is what the inspector explains (MCR-SEC-025, condition F2). Cited: content-src/raw/rhel8/chronyd.man.txt#L7 and #L68.

gen-podman-ps.pins: podman is not offered on RHEL 7; -a is a conditional bare option literal

gen-podman-stop.pins: podman is not offered on RHEL 7; the container is positional

gen-ansible-playbook.pins: the playbook generator's long options keep the '=' join; site.yml is a positional

gen-ansible-inventory.pins: -i is a SHORT option and takes its argument with a space, never '='

gen-ansible-cfg.pins: dump is a subcommand, not an option; --only-changed is a long option with no value

gen-git-clone.pins: git clone accepts repository and destination as positional operands

gen-git-branch.pins: checkout -b is supported across the covered RHEL Git generations; start is positional

gen-git-merge.pins: --no-ff is a bare long option and source is positional

gen-git-rebase.pins: upstream and optional branch are positional operands

gen-git-tag.pins: -a is bare; short -m takes its value space-joined before tag and target operands

gen-git-log.pins: --oneline and --decorate are bare; short -n takes a space-joined count

gen-git-bisect.pins: start is a subcommand; bad and good are positional revisions in that order

gen-git-recovery.pins: branch recovery creates a named ref at the lost revision without moving HEAD

gen-sshd-config.pins: syntax check reads the generated literal filename; -t and -f are separate short-option tokens

gen-chrony-config.pins: parse/print mode reads the generated literal filename; -p and -f are separate short-option tokens

gen-rsyslog-config.pins: -N1 is a literal validation mode and -f takes the generated literal filename

gen-sudoers-config.pins: -c and -f are literal validation options followed by the generated literal filename

gen-systemd-unit.pins: verify is a subcommand and the generated unit filename is a positional operand

gen-cron-config.pins: the generated filename is the positional replacement-crontab operand

grep-search-text.pins: Selected grep flags are independent option literals; the search pattern and target remain distinct quoted operands.

kill-send-signal.pins: The signal stays the curated -TERM literal; the PID uses a positive-process-ID grammar.

curl-transfer-url.pins: curl short options remain separate; -o takes the quoted output path and the URL remains a positional operand.

wget-download-url.pins: -O takes a separate quoted output path; the URL is the final positional operand.

ssh-remote-shell.pins: -i and -l take separate validated values; the hostname is a closed-grammar positional operand.

scp-secure-copy.pins: The optional -p precedes a local absolute path and a closed-grammar remote path.

rsync-sync-files.pins: Archive flags include -s/--protect-args so older remote rsync shells cannot reinterpret the validated remote path.

git-checkout-discard-changes.pins: --literal-pathspecs and -- prevent pathspec magic and option parsing; the value uses a literal repo-relative grammar.

git-recovery-wrong-branch.pins: The selected revision is one validated Git revision operand to cherry-pick.

git-recovery-lost-commit.pins: Both the new refname and recovered revision are validated and emitted as separate operands.

r-id.pins: The validated username is the only positional operand.

r-usermod-ag.pins: -a is mandatory and -G takes the quoted group list before the username operand.

export-shell-variable.pins: The shell-variable grammar accepts only a valid identifier; no value or expansion is synthesized.

tr-translate-characters.pins: -d is a curated option literal and the character set remains one quoted operand.

_flags_column: MCR-SEC-023. The flag-by-flag panel must name every option the command shows, in the order the command shows them — option tokens AND option-shaped literals ('-T', '-P', '-r', '--permanent', '--boot'). A panel silent about a flag that is present is a smaller version of a panel describing one that is not. Where no curated or dictionary explanation exists the panel says 'unverified — see man page'; it never guesses.
